messages.subject: טיפונת רשמים מכנס useR!2019
messages.body_plain:
כמה דברים שכתבתי לעצמי סביב הכנס R משבוע שעבר.
זו רשימה מאד לא ממצא, אבל מקווה שזה יתן לכם כמה רעיונות לדברים מעניינים לקרוא ולהסתכל עליהם עוד.

You can see materials from the various tutorials here: http://www.user2019.fr/tutorials/ Tutorials I took:
Di’s Visualising high-dimensional data, see: https://github.com/dicook/useR2019_highd_vis The beginning is playing around with ggplot2 (was nice, but nothing particularly new). The one thing which was new to me was the tourr R package for grand tour visualization. I’ve heard about it before, but she also talked a bit about how to interpret the tour (look at the way in which the data points move together, or not, to identify clusters and extreme points). This insight was new to me, and interesting.
Marco’s bnlearn tutorial (on probabilistic graphical models). It was much less handson, and very much an overview. All in all, it was helpful and interesting introduction to his work on bnlearn for the past 10 years. He has removed his slides from his website, but I’ve uploaded them to my dropbox, and you can grab them from here: https://www.dropbox.com/s/f9kj1ommdfstore/conf-useR19.tar.gz?dl=0
During the rest of the conference I’ve attended various sessions and talks. The keynotes talks were definitely the best part. You can download the slides to them all from here (they’ll also probably upload videos of the sessions within a week): http://www.user2019.fr/talk_schedule/ Some highlights (I mention talks that I attended and found interesting, there are more interesting talks in the schedule link above!):
n() cool #dplyr things - http://www.user2019.fr/static/pres/t257501.pdf
You don't need Spark for this - larger-than-RAM data manipulation with disk.frame - http://www.user2019.fr/static/pres/t244252.pptx (I’ve heard from the developer of the ff package that he thinks this package could probably replace his in the future. It depends on the fst package from FB)
A Generalized Framework for Parametric Regression Splines - http://www.user2019.fr/static/pres/t256357.pdf A nice implementation to more easily fit regression splines
Anomaly Detection in R - https://prital.netlify.com/talks/user2019/user2019#1
Data Science in a Box - http://www.user2019.fr/static/pres/t258008.pdf a nice project for creating teaching materials for data science with R for noobs
Visualizing multivariate linear models in R - http://www.user2019.fr/static/pres/t251298.pdf
Navigating through the R packages for movement - http://www.user2019.fr/static/pres/t258615.pdf give some sense of scope
Package flextable: a grammar to produce tabular reporting from R - http://www.user2019.fr/static/pres/t256480.pdf I really liked this one!
A missing value tour in R - http://www.user2019.fr/static/pres/keynote_201907101600.pdf great keynote! MANY resources here: https://cran.r-project.org/web/views/MissingData.html
Shiny's Holy Grail: Interactivity with reproducibility - http://www.user2019.fr/static/pres/keynote_201907110915.zip a brave first attempt at making shiny interactive. Very much work in progress...
Use aRt to learn algorithms, math, and R - http://www.user2019.fr/static/pres/lt257581.pdf short and nice
Machine Learning with R: do it with a framework - http://www.welovedatascience.com/user2019
Building and Benchmarking Automatic Machine Learning Systems - http://www.user2019.fr/static/pres/t258053.pdf autoML is cool
Discovering the cause: Tools for structure learning in R - http://www.user2019.fr/static/pres/t257340.pdf
colorspace: A Toolbox for Manipulating and Assessing Color Palettes - http://www.user2019.fr/static/pres/t253801.pdf The first time I really understood what HCL is!
How Bioconductor advances science while contributing to the R language and community - http://www.user2019.fr/static/pres/keynote_201907111600.zip bioconductor is an impressive project...
Tools for Model-Based Clustering in R - http://www.user2019.fr/static/pres/keynote_201907120915.pdf great overview of mixture models for clustering
Maximum spacing estimation, a new method in fitdistrplus - http://www.user2019.fr/static/pres/lt256822.pdf
prVis: a Novel Method for Visual Dimension Reduction - http://www.user2019.fr/static/pres/t258521.pdf very nice. This is just adding polynomial and interaction terms to X and doing PCA on that. It seems to have interesting results (as compared with tSNE etc.)
compboost: Fast and Flexible Component-Wise Boosting Framework - http://www.user2019.fr/static/pres/t257840.pdf interesting idea.
How to speed-up VSURF (Variable Selection Using Random Forests)? - http://www.user2019.fr/static/pres/t255938.pdf apparently you don’t... :(
Making sense of CRAN: Package and collaboration networks - http://ikosmidis.com/files/ikosmidis_cranly_user2019/#1 cranly is cool
The next generation of the survival package - http://www.user2019.fr/static/pres/t256796.pdf tl;dr: more events
'AI for Good' in the R and Python ecosystems - http://www.user2019.fr/static/pres/keynote_201907121415.pdf a great way to end the conference, very nice stories of using data science to solve interesting “good for the community” problems.
I very much enjoyed the conference, and especially getting to talk to many many people (there were ~1200 people this year) about R and in general. One theme that I asked people about was R vs Python, and it sounds like (at least for the people who came, which is a very biased sample), they have a lot of faith in R and intend to keep using it moving forward for many years to come.
